title: Academor SAT Practice Test 5 Reading and Writing

questions.question:
The tour guide's directions were frustratingly ____________: “Walk until you see the old tree,” he said, “then turn somewhere near the river.”

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: imprecise
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

“Somewhere near the river” is vague, so the directions were imprecise.

questions.question:
Engineers designed the stadium's roof to be ____________: it can withstand winds of more than 200 kilometers per hour and the weight of heavy snow.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: resilient
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

A roof that withstands strong winds and heavy snow is resilient.

questions.question:
The diplomat's ____________ reply—“My government will consider all options”—revealed nothing about what her country actually planned to do.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: guarded
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

An answer designed to reveal nothing is guarded.

questions.question:
Early reviews of the film were ____________: some critics called it a masterpiece, while others dismissed it as confusing and slow.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: polarized
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Opinions split into two opposite camps are polarized.

questions.question:
It is often claimed that the Great Wall of China is the only human-made structure visible from space. Astronauts who have orbited Earth, however, report that the wall is very difficult to see with the naked eye, because it is narrow and similar in color to the land around it. Large cities, highways, and airports, by contrast, are often easy to spot, especially at night.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why the Great Wall of China was built from local materials.
It presents evidence that challenges the claim in the first sentence.
It offers an example that supports the claim in the first sentence.
It describes the equipment that astronauts use to photograph Earth.
questions.correct: It presents evidence that challenges the claim in the first sentence.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Astronauts' reports that the wall is hard to see undercut the common claim.

questions.question:
Louis Braille lost his sight as a young child. As a student at a school for blind children in Paris, he learned about “night writing,” a system of raised dots designed for soldiers to read in the dark. The system used cells of up to twelve dots, which were too large to feel with a single fingertip. By the age of fifteen, Braille had developed a simpler system based on cells of only six dots, which readers could recognize with one touch. A version of his system is still used around the world.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To explain how Louis Braille created his reading system by improving an existing one
To argue that night writing was more useful to soldiers than Braille's system
To describe the school in Paris where Louis Braille later taught
To compare the reading speeds of people who use different dot systems
questions.correct: To explain how Louis Braille created his reading system by improving an existing one
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The text traces how Braille simplified the twelve-dot night writing into his six-dot system.

questions.question:
Text 1

Some educators argue that students learn more when they take notes by hand than when they type them on a laptop. Because writing is slower than typing, they explain, students who write by hand must summarize what they hear instead of copying it word for word.

Text 2

Education researcher Marco Bianchi compared students who took notes by hand with students who typed notes after being told to summarize rather than to record every word. Both groups remembered the material equally well. Bianchi concludes that what matters is how students take notes, not what they use to take them.

Based on the texts, how would Bianchi (Text 2) most likely respond to the educators' argument in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that students who type notes always remember less than students who write by hand
By suggesting that the benefit they attribute to handwriting comes from summarizing, which students can also do while typing
By arguing that summarizing is less useful than recording every word
By claiming that writing by hand is faster than typing for most students
questions.correct: By suggesting that the benefit they attribute to handwriting comes from summarizing, which students can also do while typing
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Bianchi found that typists who summarized did as well, so the key factor is summarizing, not handwriting.

questions.question:
Ocean tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon, which draws the water on the side of Earth facing it into a bulge. The Sun's gravity also affects the tides, though less strongly because the Sun is much farther away. When the Sun and Moon line up, as they do at new and full moon, their pulls combine to produce especially large tides, called spring tides.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The Sun's gravity has a stronger effect on tides than the Moon's gravity does.
Spring tides occur only during the spring months of the year.
Tides are produced mostly by the Moon's gravity, with the Sun's gravity adding to the effect, especially when the two are aligned.
Tides are caused by winds that push ocean water toward the shore.
questions.correct: Tides are produced mostly by the Moon's gravity, with the Sun's gravity adding to the effect, especially when the two are aligned.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The text explains the Moon's main role, the Sun's smaller one, and their combined effect.

questions.question:
The following text is from a short story. Ana's father, a fisherman, has injured his hand.

For years Ana had watched him mend the nets on the dock, his fingers moving faster than she could follow. Now he sat beside her with his bandaged hand in his lap and talked her through it: over, under, pull the knot tight. Her first knots slipped. By evening they held, and her father, who was not a man who gave compliments, tested one with his good hand and simply nodded.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Ana refuses to help her father mend the nets.
Ana learns a skill from her injured father and earns his quiet approval.
Ana's father is unable to explain how to mend the nets.
Ana's father criticizes the knots that Ana ties at the end of the day.
questions.correct: Ana learns a skill from her injured father and earns his quiet approval.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Ana learns to mend the nets with her father's guidance, and his nod shows approval.

questions.question:
Agronomist Lucia Ferraro and her team claim that a new organic fertilizer substantially increases the amount of wheat that a field produces.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the researchers' claim?
options: Farmers who tried the new fertilizer said it was easy to apply.
The new fertilizer costs slightly more than older fertilizers.
Wheat grown with the new fertilizer was slightly taller on average.
In the same region and season, fields treated with the new fertilizer produced about the same amount of wheat as similar fields that received no fertilizer.
questions.correct: In the same region and season, fields treated with the new fertilizer produced about the same amount of wheat as similar fields that received no fertilizer.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

If treated fields produced no more than untreated ones, the claim of increased yield is weakened.

questions.question:
A report on volunteering in Linton notes that adults in the middle of their working lives were the most likely to volunteer: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: 24% of adults aged 18 to 29 volunteered, the lowest percentage of any age group.
28% of adults aged 65 and older volunteered.
31% of adults aged 30 to 44 volunteered, a higher percentage than in any other age group.
36% of adults aged 45 to 64 volunteered, a higher percentage than in any other age group.
questions.correct: 36% of adults aged 45 to 64 volunteered, a higher percentage than in any other age group.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The 45–64 group had the highest share, which supports the report's statement.

questions.question:
An energy analyst notes that the number of electric cars registered in Country P grew rapidly, more than doubling every two years between 2016 and 2022: the number rose from ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: about 190 thousand in 2022 to about 75 thousand in 2020.
about 12 thousand in 2016 to about 15 thousand in 2018.
about 12 thousand in 2016 to about 30 thousand in 2018 and about 75 thousand in 2020.
about 75 thousand in 2018 to about 190 thousand in 2020.
questions.correct: about 12 thousand in 2016 to about 30 thousand in 2018 and about 75 thousand in 2020.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

12 to 30 and 30 to 75 are each more than a doubling, and the years match the graph.

questions.question:
Marine biologists transplanted fragments of coral at four depths to help restore a damaged reef. They concluded that fragments survived best at intermediate depths: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
options: the same number of fragments was planted at each depth.
68% and 71% of fragments survived at 6 and 9 meters, compared with 42% at 3 meters and 39% at 12 meters.
fewer fragments survived at 12 meters than at any other depth.
questions.correct: 68% and 71% of fragments survived at 6 and 9 meters, compared with 42% at 3 meters and 39% at 12 meters.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Only this choice compares the middle depths with both the shallowest and the deepest.

questions.question:
Wild wheat plants scatter their seeds when the seeds are ripe, but cultivated wheat keeps its seeds attached until they are harvested. At an archaeological site about 10,000 years old, researchers found that the oldest layers contained mostly wheat with the wild, scattering trait, while later layers contained more and more wheat that kept its seeds. These findings suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: wild wheat stopped growing near the site 10,000 years ago.
the people at the site ate less wheat as time went on.
people at the site may have gradually begun to cultivate wheat over time.
cultivated wheat was brought to the site from elsewhere all at once.
questions.correct: people at the site may have gradually begun to cultivate wheat over time.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

A gradual rise in the cultivated trait across layers points to cultivation developing over time.

questions.question:
The number of students taking the advanced chemistry course ____________ increased every year since the school built its new laboratory.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: has
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

“The number” is singular, so the verb is has; “since” calls for the present perfect.

questions.question:
The tour visited three cities: Lyon, ____________ Turin, Italy; and Geneva, Switzerland.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: France;
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

When items in a list contain commas, semicolons separate the items.

questions.question:
Each of the cities that applied to host the conference had to describe how ____________ would provide housing for visitors.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: it
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The pronoun refers to “each,” which is singular, so it is required.

questions.question:
Mae Jemison was the first African American woman to travel into ____________ in 1992 she flew aboard the space shuttle Endeavour.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: space;
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Two independent clauses are joined with a semicolon.

questions.question:
The paintings in the new exhibit are brighter than ____________ in the museum's permanent collection.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: those
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Paintings must be compared with other paintings; the plural pronoun those does this.

questions.question:
The scientists faced an unexpected ____________ the samples they had collected in the Arctic had thawed during shipping.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: problem:
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

A colon introduces the explanation of the problem; a comma alone would create a comma splice.

questions.question:
Whoever finishes the puzzle first ____________ the prize, a book of even harder puzzles.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: wins
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

“Whoever finishes the puzzle first” is a singular subject, so the verb is wins.

questions.question:
Honeybees communicate the location of food through dances. ____________ a bee that has found flowers far from the hive performs a “waggle dance” whose angle points other bees toward the food.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.correct: For example,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The waggle dance is an example of communication through dance.

questions.question:
Many early cars ran on electricity. ____________ by the 1920s, cars powered by gasoline had become far more common, partly because gasoline was cheap and the cars could travel long distances.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.correct: However,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The rise of gasoline cars contrasts with the early popularity of electric cars.

questions.question:
The team's first prototype was too heavy to fly. ____________ the engineers replaced its metal frame with one made of carbon fiber, cutting its weight by more than half.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.correct: To solve this problem,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Replacing the frame responds to the weight problem.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The Panama Canal opened in 1914.
  • It connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans across the Isthmus of Panama.
  • Before it opened, ships traveling between New York and San Francisco had to sail around the southern tip of South America.
  • The canal shortened that trip by about 13,000 kilometers.

The student wants to emphasize how the Panama Canal changed shipping.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Panama Canal crosses the Isthmus of Panama.
Before 1914, ships sailed around the southern tip of South America.
By connecting the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, the Panama Canal shortened the voyage between New York and San Francisco by about 13,000 kilometers.
questions.correct: By connecting the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, the Panama Canal shortened the voyage between New York and San Francisco by about 13,000 kilometers.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Only this choice shows the canal's effect on shipping.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Cheetahs can run at about 100 kilometers per hour.
  • They can keep up that speed for only about 20 to 30 seconds.
  • Pronghorn antelope can run at about 90 kilometers per hour.
  • Pronghorn can keep up high speeds for several minutes.

The student wants to contrast the running abilities of cheetahs and pronghorn.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Although cheetahs are slightly faster than pronghorn, pronghorn can keep up high speeds for much longer.
Cheetahs can run at about 100 kilometers per hour.
Pronghorn can run at about 90 kilometers per hour and keep up high speeds for several minutes.
Both cheetahs and pronghorn are fast runners.
questions.correct: Although cheetahs are slightly faster than pronghorn, pronghorn can keep up high speeds for much longer.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Only this choice contrasts speed and endurance across the two animals.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Frida Kahlo was a Mexican painter born in 1907.
  • Many of her best-known works are self-portraits.
  • Her paintings often combine images from Mexican folk art with personal symbols.
  • In 1938 she held her first solo exhibition, in New York City.

The student wants to describe the style of Kahlo's paintings.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Frida Kahlo was a Mexican painter born in 1907.
Frida Kahlo's paintings, many of them self-portraits, often combine images from Mexican folk art with personal symbols.
In 1938 Frida Kahlo held her first solo exhibition, in New York City.
Frida Kahlo held an exhibition in New York City.
questions.correct: Frida Kahlo's paintings, many of them self-portraits, often combine images from Mexican folk art with personal symbols.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Only this choice describes her style.

questions.question:
The biologist was ____________ about her results, cautioning reporters that her sample was small and that the findings would need to be confirmed by other studies.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: circumspect
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Warning that the findings are limited shows caution: she was circumspect.

questions.question:
The novel's ____________ plot, which jumps back and forth across three centuries and a dozen narrators, rewards careful readers but frustrates casual ones.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: convoluted
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

A plot that jumps across centuries and narrators is complicated, or convoluted.

questions.question:
Little remains of the medieval castle, which was gradually ____________ by later residents of the town, who took its stones to build their own houses and walls.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: dismantled
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Taking the castle's stones away piece by piece dismantled it.

questions.question:
The new evidence did not ____________ the theory; it simply showed that the theory applies to fewer cases than its supporters had claimed.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: invalidate
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The evidence limited the theory without disproving it, so it did not invalidate it.

questions.question:
In 1977 a severe drought struck Daphne Major, a small island in the Galápagos. Most of the plants that produce small, soft seeds died, leaving mainly large, hard seeds. Biologists Peter and Rosemary Grant, who had been measuring the island's finches for years, found that many birds died during the drought. The survivors had, on average, larger beaks, which allowed them to crack the hard seeds. The next generation of finches also had larger beaks than the generation before the drought.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It compares two species of finches and argues that one is better suited to drought.
It explains how the Grants chose Daphne Major and then describes their measuring methods.
It describes an environmental change and then explains how that change affected the physical traits of a bird population.
It describes a drought and then argues that the finches will eventually leave the island.
questions.correct: It describes an environmental change and then explains how that change affected the physical traits of a bird population.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The text moves from the drought, to its effect on seeds, to the survival of larger-beaked finches and their offspring.

questions.question:
Bioluminescence, the production of light by living things, is rare on land but common in the deep sea. In one large survey of the open ocean, about three-quarters of the animals observed between the surface and a depth of nearly 4,000 meters could produce their own light. They use it to attract prey, to find mates, and to confuse predators.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains how animals produce light.
It describes the uses of bioluminescence on land.
It provides support for the statement that bioluminescence is common in the deep sea.
It questions estimates of how many animals live in the deep sea.
questions.correct: It provides support for the statement that bioluminescence is common in the deep sea.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The survey finding of about three-quarters supports the claim that the trait is common in the sea.

questions.question:
Text 1

Some economists argue that raising a city's minimum wage will lead businesses to cut jobs, because employers will hire fewer workers when each worker costs more.

Text 2

Economist Hana Kim studied restaurants in neighboring towns, one of which raised its minimum wage. Over three years, employment at restaurants in that town did not fall compared with the other town. Kim notes that higher wages also reduced how often workers quit, which saved employers the cost of hiring and training new staff.

Based on the texts, how would Kim (Text 2) most likely respond to the economists' argument in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that raising the minimum wage always leads businesses to cut jobs
By noting that it leaves out savings that can offset the cost of higher wages
By claiming that restaurants in both towns hired more workers than they needed
By arguing that the minimum wage should be the same in every town
questions.correct: By noting that it leaves out savings that can offset the cost of higher wages
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Kim found no job losses and points to savings from lower turnover, which the economists do not consider.

questions.question:
For most of the twentieth century, scientists believed that adult birds could not grow new brain cells. In the 1980s, however, neuroscientist Fernando Nottebohm found that canaries grow large numbers of new neurons in the brain regions that control song, especially in the season when they learn new songs. His work helped convince researchers to look for new neuron growth in other animals, including mammals.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Canaries learn new songs only when they are young.
A study of canaries challenged a long-held belief about adult brains and encouraged further research on the topic.
Scientists have proven that adult mammals cannot grow new neurons.
Birds grow new brain cells in every region of the brain at the same rate.
questions.correct: A study of canaries challenged a long-held belief about adult brains and encouraged further research on the topic.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The discovery overturned an assumption and led researchers to look for similar growth elsewhere.

questions.question:
The following text is from a short story. Mr. Petrov, a retired teacher, is visiting his old school.

The classroom had new desks, and the chalkboard had been replaced by a white screen that glowed when the teacher touched it. Mr. Petrov felt like a guest in a house he used to own. Then a boy in the front row raised his hand and asked the same question Mr. Petrov had been asked every year for thirty-five years—why do we have to learn this?—and the old teacher smiled, because the answer had not changed.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although the classroom has changed, Mr. Petrov recognizes something familiar in the students.
Mr. Petrov is upset that the school has removed the chalkboard.
Mr. Petrov cannot answer the student's question about learning.
Mr. Petrov decides to return to teaching at his old school.
questions.correct: Although the classroom has changed, Mr. Petrov recognizes something familiar in the students.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The new equipment makes him feel like a guest, but a familiar question reconnects him to the classroom.

questions.question:
Linguist Amaru Quispe claims that children who grow up hearing two languages learn to tell apart the sounds of each language very early, before they can speak either language.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers' claim?
options: Eight-month-old infants raised with two languages noticed when a speaker switched from one language to the other, while infants raised with one language did not.
Children raised with two languages usually speak their first words at the same age as other children.
Adults who learned a second language as children have larger vocabularies than other adults.
Many parents who speak two languages use only one language with their children.
questions.correct: Eight-month-old infants raised with two languages noticed when a speaker switched from one language to the other, while infants raised with one language did not.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Infants who cannot yet speak noticing a switch between languages directly supports the claim.

questions.question:
A media researcher surveyed adults about how much they trust different sources of news. The researcher notes that the gap between younger and older respondents was largest for television news: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: 52% of respondents aged 55 and older trusted local newspapers a great deal, compared with 38% of those aged 18 to 34.
18% of respondents aged 18 to 34 trusted social media a great deal.
44% of respondents aged 55 and older trusted television news a great deal, compared with 26% of those aged 18 to 34.
26% of respondents aged 55 and older trusted television news a great deal, compared with 44% of those aged 18 to 34.
questions.correct: 44% of respondents aged 55 and older trusted television news a great deal, compared with 26% of those aged 18 to 34.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The television gap (18 points) is the largest; the last choice reverses the groups.

questions.question:
A pesticide that builds up in fish was banned in the region around Lake Mira in 1990. Scientists say that the ban has worked, but slowly, because the pesticide that had already entered the lake breaks down over decades. The graph supports this view: the pesticide level in fish ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: dropped to its lowest level in 1990, the year the ban took effect.
has risen steadily every year since 1980.
kept rising until about 2000 and has fallen only gradually since then.
questions.correct: kept rising until about 2000 and has fallen only gradually since then.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

A rise until about 2000 and a slow decline afterward match a delayed, gradual effect of the ban.

questions.question:
In a study, adults spent 60 minutes a week for six weeks practicing typing, divided in different ways. The researchers concluded that spreading the same amount of practice over more, shorter sessions produced better results: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
options: participants who practiced in six 10-minute sessions typed 51 words per minute, compared with 38 for those who practiced in one 60-minute session.
every group practiced for a total of 60 minutes per week.
participants who practiced in one 60-minute session typed 38 words per minute.
participants who practiced in three 20-minute sessions typed faster than those who practiced in six 10-minute sessions.
questions.correct: participants who practiced in six 10-minute sessions typed 51 words per minute, compared with 38 for those who practiced in one 60-minute session.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Only this choice compares more, shorter sessions with one long session.

questions.question:
Sound travels about four times faster in water than in air, and low-pitched sounds can travel thousands of kilometers through the ocean. Marine biologist Ines Kowalczyk recorded the calls of fin whales, which are among the lowest-pitched sounds made by any animal, and found that whales separated by hundreds of kilometers appeared to change direction in response to one another's calls. Her findings suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: fin whales may be able to communicate with one another across very long distances.
fin whales cannot hear high-pitched sounds.
sound travels more slowly in cold water than in warm water.
fin whales call most often when they are close together.
questions.correct: fin whales may be able to communicate with one another across very long distances.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Whales far apart reacting to each other's low calls suggests long-distance communication.

questions.question:
The longest river in Africa, the ____________ flows north through eleven countries before reaching the Mediterranean Sea.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: Nile,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

“The Nile” is an appositive renaming “the longest river,” so it is set off by commas on both sides.

questions.question:
The committee members, along with their chair, ____________ expected to vote on the budget tomorrow.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: are
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The subject is “members”; “along with their chair” does not change the number, so the verb is are.

questions.question:
Many people know that Benjamin Franklin experimented with ____________ fewer know that he also invented a musical instrument called the glass armonica.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: electricity;
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Two independent clauses are joined with a semicolon.

questions.question:
Neither of the two proposals ____________ enough support to pass when the council voted last week.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: had
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

“Neither” is singular, and the vote was last week, so the past tense had is correct.

questions.question:
The recipe was handed down from my great-grandmother, a baker who ran a small shop in ____________ and it has been made in our family for more than a century.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: Naples,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The appositive “a baker who ran a small shop in Naples” must end with a comma before “and it has been …”

questions.question:
After hiking for six hours, ____________

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the lake at the top of the valley finally came into view of the group.
the group finally reached the lake at the top of the valley.
the top of the valley was where the group finally found the lake.
reaching the lake at the top of the valley finally happened for the group.
questions.correct: the group finally reached the lake at the top of the valley.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The group did the hiking, so “the group” must follow the opening phrase.

questions.question:
The coach told the players that ____________ would need to practice twice a day before the championship.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: they
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The players are the subject of “would need,” so the subject pronoun they is needed.

questions.question:
Octopuses can change the color of their skin in a fraction of a second. ____________ they can change its texture, raising small bumps to look like rock or coral.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.correct: Moreover,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Changing texture adds a second ability to the first.

questions.question:
The museum's attendance fell sharply during the renovation. ____________ it rose to record levels in the year after the new galleries opened.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.correct: Afterward, though,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The record attendance after reopening contrasts with the earlier fall.

questions.question:
The experiment's results were clear: plants given more light grew faster. ____________ plants given the most light grew about twice as tall as those given the least.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.correct: In particular,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The second sentence gives a specific detail of the general result.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The axolotl is a salamander native to lakes near Mexico City.
  • Unlike most salamanders, it usually keeps its gills and lives in water its whole life.
  • Axolotls can regrow lost limbs, parts of their spinal cord, and even parts of their heart.
  • Scientists study axolotls to learn more about how tissues regenerate.

The student wants to explain why scientists study axolotls.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The axolotl is a salamander native to lakes near Mexico City.
